comparator.name: European Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official UvA study-programme page and 2026–27 Course Catalogue establish a 180-EC, three-year European Studies bachelor. The shared first year is 60 EC: 36 EC of European history, integration, democracy, identity and culture plus four 6-EC modern-language proficiency modules. In years 2 and 3 students take one 48-EC major, Philosophy of the Humanities (6 EC), 24 EC of programme-related electives, 30 EC of free choice and a 12-EC bachelor thesis. The first-listed European Culture major is selected as the neutral route before considering UCR fit. The aggregate major and open choice spaces are retained without inventing internal courses.
components: Constructing Europe: History, Culture and Politics
Coming Together, Coming Apart: Theories and Processes of European Integration and Enlargement
The first-listed official major is selected neutrally; the catalogue publishes the major as a coherent 48-EC route.
Free electives, minor, exchange or internship

routeSelection.basis: The programme requires one of six 48-EC majors and lists European Culture first. No target-specific evidence privileges a student route, so the first-listed major is used neutrally before the UCR comparison. All official majors remain assessed as candidate directions.

core: European political and cultural history, identities, nationalism, imperialism and historical interpretation
European integration, democracy, institutions, borders, enlargement and international relations
European economics, the internal market and the effects of economic decisions
Multilingual and comparative study of European societies, power, representation and equality
Academic writing, comparative analysis and independent research in European Studies
adjacent: European Culture and European History as named major directions
European Law and European Politics as named major directions
European Economics as a named major direction
East European Studies as a named regional direction
questions: How integration, borders and institutions shape European democracy and crises
How historical ideas and identities shape contemporary Europe
How power, representation and inequality operate across European societies

alternatives.label: European politics, integration and political economy
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines European Union politics with comparative politics, international relations, public law, economics, history and social research; its visible label states this sustained political-institutional and political-economic centre.
alternatives.concept: Builds a broad European Studies pathway around EU politics, comparative institutions, law, political economy, international relations, history and social change. It is the closest UCR approximation to the programme-wide study of Europe while remaining less regionally and linguistically specialised than UvA.
progression: No UCR course in this alternative carries a formal prerequisite except the courses that require GOSGATE102 (GOSLAWJ212, GOSLAWJ213, GOSLAWJ312) and BENGATE102 (BENECON211, BENECON212, BENECON312, BENECON311); GOSGATE102 is scheduled in semester 1 and BENGATE102 in semester 2, each before every course that depends on it. Personal & Professional Development is scheduled in semester 2, within Year 1. Introductory Year-1 courses (Law Society & Justice, Introduction to Political Philosophy, Foundations of Comparative Politics, Introduction to Economics) are concentrated in semester 1, and level-3 advanced work (Public Economics, Comparative Constitutional Law's prerequisite chain, European Union Politics, Persuasive Communication, Econometrics, Peace & Conflict, Foundations of European Union Law) is concentrated in semesters 4-6, so foundational training precedes advanced work. Where an advisory continuation exists in the course evidence, it is honoured: Research Methods & Statistics (semester 2) precedes the more advanced Econometrics (semester 6); The Art of Rhetorical Communication (semester 3) precedes the more advanced Persuasive Communication (semester 5); and Theory of International Relations (semester 2) precedes the more advanced European Union Politics (semester 5) and Peace & Conflict (semester 6). Every course is offered in its assigned semester under the fixed Fall 2026 cohort schedule.

alternatives.label: European culture, identity and political representation
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is dominated by culture, media, identity, representation, society and political power, supported by comparative methods and history.
alternatives.concept: Develops the named European Culture and European History directions through cultural and media analysis, sociology, comparative politics, rhetoric, identity, representation and historical context. It treats Europe as a contested cultural and political construction rather than primarily as an institutional system.
progression: Communication, media, sociology, politics, psychology and qualitative and quantitative foundations precede advanced persuasion, organisational culture, media analysis, political study and creative production. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass, with nine 300-level courses.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route replaces extensive economics, law, international relations and historical-institutional study with media, rhetoric, social psychology, cultural production, entrepreneurship and advanced communication. It therefore changes both the disciplinary mix and the object of study from European governance to cultural identity and representation.

alternatives.label: European law, institutions and democratic justice
alternatives.concept: Concentrates the named European Law and European Politics directions around EU law, comparative constitutional law, human rights, international justice, political institutions, public argument and social equality. Economics remains supporting context rather than the programme’s organizing field.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is structured around public, international and EU law, political institutions, democracy, justice and social contestation.
progression: Law, Society & Justice precedes all formally dependent 200/300-level law courses; Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations precedes Transnational Business Law. Comparative politics and sociology foundations precede advanced EU politics and social theory, and all course offerings and formal prerequisites are satisfied.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route replaces a substantial share of economics, business, political-economy and history courses with criminal justice, human rights, comparative constitutional law, EU law, international law, sociology, philosophy and environmental justice. Compared with the culture route, it replaces media, cultural production and communication with a sustained public-law and institutions sequence.

blocks: Both directly examine EU institutions, European integration and democratic governance.
Both address the legal and institutional architecture of European integration and cross-border governance.
Both examine European political and cultural history and connect historical interpretation to contemporary Europe.
Both analyse collective identities, representation and social contestation in contemporary societies.
Both support sustained advanced cultural analysis of representation, identity and public meaning.
Both provide philosophical analysis of values, arguments and the foundations of humanistic inquiry.

selection.assessment: The broad closest match covers the programme-defining study of European integration, politics, history, identity and political economy. European Culture/History and European Law/Politics/Economics support two coherent, feasible and pairwise distinct additional curricula. East European Studies lacks enough region-specific UCR depth for another defensible programme. Production stops at the maximum of three alternatives.

notes.text: The selected European Culture major is represented as the official 48-EC aggregate; internal courses and credit allocations are not invented.

UvA requires four modern-language proficiency modules. UCR has no equivalent language sequence, so those components remain unmatched rather than being replaced by general linguistics or intercultural courses.

UvA combines a shared European Studies core, language sequence and one named 48-EC major. UCR distributes related work across a student-designed interdisciplinary Liberal Arts and Sciences curriculum.
